page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel processors, which map to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

The underlying Intel CPU includes an L3 cache of 260 MB, alongside 2 MB of L2 cache and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and 8-bit integer operations. In performance testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, scoring 1886.0 in Geekbench single-core benchmarks and 2396.0 in text processing. Multi-core performance is characterized as average, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 14630.37 and a Passmark CPU score of 21470.49.

Memory performance is supported by a cached small-block read bandwidth of 1133.53 GB/sec, which drops to 130.97 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves an average static web serving throughput of 25.59 GB/sec and handles 17.79 million Redis SET operations per second. Large-model LLM inference is constrained by the lack of GPU acceleration and the 32 GB memory capacity, though it processes prompts for a small 135M model at 1272.6 tokens/sec. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints, making it suitable for software compilation, web serving, and moderate computational workloads.

Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance is designed for CPU-intensive workloads. It features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1886.0 and strong text processing capabilities. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Passmark CPU score of 21470.49 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 14630.37. Memory bandwidth reaches 1133.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks. This hardware profile provides a cost-efficient resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it highly suitable for software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight vector or matrix operations.
